image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a reusable cloth diaper. The main body is made of a soft, white, textured fabric (likely fleece or microfiber). It features blue patterned trim along the top waistband and leg openings. Yellow elastic loops are visible on the sides, likely part of the fastening system. A small red and black tag with text is sewn onto the lower left side. The diaper appears bulky and padded.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rectangular when flat, with elasticized leg openings and waistband.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object clearly displays elasticized leg openings (gathered ruffles) and a defined waistband area, consistent with the structural geometry of a diaper.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Thickness is notably padded and bulky when uncompressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The folds and shadows indicate significant thickness and padding, characteristic of an absorbent core.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Folded form shows layered construction with absorbent core between layers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The diaper is assembled/closed; the internal layered construction of the core is not directly visible from this exterior view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Fastening system uses adhesive tabs (hook-and-loop or sticky) on side panels.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Yellow elastic loops/straps are visible on the sides, indicating a fastening mechanism typical of cloth diapers (snap or loop-based).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elastic creates gathered ruffles at leg cuffs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct gathering/ruffling is visible along the leg holes, caused by elastic casing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Size indicators and wetness strip may be visible.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No wetness indicator strip is visible. There is a brand tag, but it does not appear to be a size indicator in the traditional sense, nor is it clearly readable as such.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Outer surface is smooth plastic or fabric-like material in white or printed patterns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The outer surface is a white, textured fabric (fleece-like), fitting the 'fabric-like material' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Inner surface is soft non-woven fabric.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The inner lining is not exposed in this view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Absorbent padded core with waterproof outer layer.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the padding is implied by bulk, the specific 'waterproof' nature of the outer layer cannot be visually confirmed vs just water-resistant fabric, and the core itself is hidden.

artifact_observations.location: Red tag on lower left side
artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the small red tag is illegible and blurry. While common in real photos due to resolution, in AI generation this often represents a failure to render coherent text. It looks like plausible branding but lacks distinct characters.

The texture is very uniform and slightly 'noisy' or 'smudged' in the highlights, lacking the distinct individual fiber definition expected in a macro shot of fleece. It borders on looking like a generated noise pattern rather than physical fabric grain.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific sub-type (reusable cloth vs disposable) and verify class alignment.
To check for melting or fusion artifacts where the elastic gathers meet the main body, a common failure point in AI-generated clothing.
To rigorously analyze the illegible text on the tag to determine if it is gibberish or just low-resolution real text.
To assess the naturalness of the lighting and fabric texture, checking for subtle AI-smoothing artifacts.

focus_areas: Leg cuff elasticity and gathering realism
Structural plausibility of the side fasteners
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact on the tag. If the image_text_auditor confirms it is nonsensical, increase artifact severity. Also, evaluate if the uniformity of the white fabric texture suggests AI smoothing rather than optical blur.
